title: End-of-page menu morph follows your scroll instead of locking it (phones)
problem: At the end of the page, on a phone, the page takes over your scroll: once you reach the bottom, it cancels your finger's moves, pins the page in place every frame, and plays a 680 ms spring that grows the small nav pill into the dark panel (the 'morph'). Your finger stops scrolling the page for that moment.
idea: On touch phones only, the page gets one extra screen of scroll after the last section. The last section (#platform) stays put (CSS sticky) while that screen scrolls in, and the morph value is simply how far it has scrolled in, 0 to 1. So the panel opens and closes with your finger, like a normal scroll. Nothing cancels touch moves, nothing pins the page, no spring runs. Light snapping (CSS scroll-snap 'proximity') pulls a rest near closed or near open to the end. Rev 2: built directly on the current best build v7, without the morph-on-GPU change (morph-gpu rev 2 A measured slower on the phone, P-098) and without its early layer prep. Desktop, tablets and reduced motion keep today's behaviour. Base (A, v7): js 8c90da217745, css 308f0da70c3a; this (B): js d661831b8797, css cff335191762.
looksSame: No. The motion is new: the panel follows the finger instead of a fixed spring, and it can rest half open (see the differences). Still frames at the same morph value match the base in the iOS Simulator while the panel covers the last section (only the running countdown differs, in base vs base too). Where the last section shows, Safari draws its text about 1 device pixel higher (T3, below). In Chrome only the EN language label differs (below).
visualDiff: Motion: the morph follows your scroll position, not a 680 ms spring. Scroll halfway and the panel is halfway open.
Half-open rest is possible: Safari snaps a 'proximity' point only within 0.3 of the screen height (WebKit source, CONFIRMED), so a rest between about 30 % and 70 % open stays there.
Option if you want it: settle to the nearer end when the finger lets go (not built).

Safari only, T3 (over the wide rule by share, not by shade): wherever the last section (#platform) is on screen, its text and edges sit about 1 device pixel (1/3 CSS px) higher. Closed at the end: 0.89 % of the screen over 8 shades, max 77. One screen before: 0.57 %, max 78. Base vs base: 0.
Why (Safari): the box position is identical to 1/64 px. WebKit gives every sticky box its own GPU layer (WebKit source, CONFIRMED); that this layer causes the 1 px shift is OBSERVED, cause unknown.
Safari, panel covering the section (m 0.25 to 1): equal to the base apart from the countdown, which also differs base vs base (max shade 224 in both).

Chrome: the EN language label at the top right differs at every morph value, about 600 device px (0.02 %), max shade 187; everything else equals the base. Base vs base was 0 there in this run (rev 1 saw the same label differ base vs base). OBSERVED, cause unknown.
The page is one screen longer on phones.
Nothing changes on desktop, tablets or with reduced motion.

gain.what: Touch moves cancelled at the end of the page
gain.how: By the code: under the phone gate the listener is never added. Checked in Chrome; the Simulator check scrolled by script only.

gain.what: Per-frame scroll pin and spring loop during the morph
gain.how: By the code and the Simulator scroll-step check on rev 2 (31 steps: morph value = scroll position, section held at the screen bottom every step).

gain.what: Smoothness and feel on the iPhone
gain.how: Needs a phone slot: the whole-page fast-flick gesture check (T-113) before it can join a best build, and your blind swipe A/B. Also untested: Safari's toolbar collapsing mid-scroll, and whether the scroll callback runs every frame during a finger scroll.

risk: A motion change: you decide whether the end-of-page morph should follow the finger. Repaint (corrected in rev 3): one big repaint (about 1.6 million pixels) in the frame where the menu leaves closed and again where it returns to closed, a snap back to closed included; the frames in between repaint only small areas (fix-morph-gpu's Simulator counts, F-223, OBSERVED). Following your scroll, that big frame comes every time you cross closed, so more often than the spring's one opening per visit. Not measured on the phone. A half-open rest can happen (WebKit's snap range, CONFIRMED). In Safari the last section is drawn 1 device px higher wherever it shows (T3), and it is its own GPU layer for the whole visit (memory not measured). Checked only with scripted scrolls in Chrome and the iOS Simulator, with the toolbar shown; no finger or gesture run yet, no reduced motion in Safari, no iPad, no rubber-band check. It reuses fix-nav-morph's setter and gate: if accepted it becomes a conflict cluster with nav-morph, and the nav-hit-cache change would need one extra line (__nsForce) to keep the nav colour right.
